reviews.counterevidence: Splitting at Ezek.41.7 or 41.9 was rejected because widening stories and foundation measurements explain the same side-chamber structure whose access and free-space arrangement conclude in 41:11.

reviews.rationale: Rear-building dimensions broaden into a summary of the completed complex and its architectural surfaces before the explicit cherub-and-palm decoration begins at 41:18, yielding a defensible 41:17 close.
reviews.support: Accept Ezek.41.12-17 as the structural-measurement child, with 41:15/16 retained as an internal seam. The clean form change is at 41:18, where decorative motifs become the controlling subject.
reviews.counterevidence: A competing stop at Ezek.41.15 was rejected because the description continues grammatically into 41:16-17; starting decoration there would sever thresholds and wall surfaces from their measured structure.

reviews.rationale: Decoration and movable or fitted furnishings replace structural dimensions as the organizing function, and the inventory carries from repeated wall motifs to altar, doors, windows, and porch ornament.
reviews.support: Keep Ezek.41.18-26 as the decoration-and-furnishing child under the larger 41:12-26 station. Its form begins with carved figures, not with the preceding measurement summary.
reviews.counterevidence: Beginning this furnishing inventory at Ezek.41.16 was rejected because 41:16-17 still completes measured architectural surfaces; the first unmistakable decorative subject arrives with cherubim in 41:18.

reviews.rationale: Mirrored chamber architecture and its cultic use form question and answer within one station: spatial descriptions establish the rooms, and 42:13-14 assigns their eating, storage, and vesting purposes.
reviews.support: Retain Ezek.42.1-14 as chamber survey plus function. North and south blocks can be internally indexed, but neither the architecture nor the priestly rules should surface without the other.
reviews.counterevidence: A cut before the functional explanation at Ezek.42.13 was rejected because the priestly uses identify why the just-measured chambers are holy; detaching function would impoverish both pieces.

reviews.rationale: Exit movement resets the station, four parallel measurements create a complete enclosure, and the final separation clause interprets the wall; together they form one four-sided survey.
reviews.support: Keep Ezek.42.15-20 as the perimeter close to the preceding interior survey. Directional items are not standalone units, because the concluding boundary function depends on all four sides.
reviews.counterevidence: Four chunks keyed to the directional repetitions in Ezek.42.16-19 were rejected because the equal sides are list members whose combined perimeter and function are stated only in 42:20.

reviews.rationale: Vision, divine presence, ethical correction, shame, architectural disclosure, and the summit-law statement create one climax, though the movement from manifestation to commission is substantial enough to hold.
reviews.support: Retain Ezek.43.1-12 provisionally and preserve the 43:5 and 43:9 alternatives for external review. The commission explains the purpose of the returning-glory scene rather than merely following it.
reviews.counterevidence: Possible endings at Ezek.43.5 after the filling or at 43.9 after the defilement warning remain live, but neither was adopted because 43:10-12 turns witnessed glory into the commanded report.

reviews.rationale: Every clause in 43:13-17 answers what the altar is shaped and sized like; priest, blood, animals, days, and acceptance do not enter until the new speech in the next verse.
reviews.support: Accept Ezek.43.13-17 as the altar specification child. Mandatory adjacency to 43:18-27 preserves function, while the shift from dimensions to enacted consecration supports the child seam.
reviews.counterevidence: Merging these measurements directly into the consecration rites of Ezek.43.18-27 was rejected for active retrieval because 43:18 opens a fresh address naming the altar's ordinances and offerings.

reviews.rationale: This passage is procedural rather than descriptive: actors, sacrificial materials, locations, repeated days, and the final divine acceptance form a complete consecration instruction.
reviews.support: Keep Ezek.43.18-27 as the ritual sibling of the measured altar. Its beginning is marked by a speech reset, and its ending is the eighth-day transition to accepted regular service.
reviews.counterevidence: Folding Ezek.43.18-27 back into the preceding dimensional list was rejected because the new address and imperative ritual sequence change both discourse mode and immediate function.

reviews.rationale: Place, object, rationale, and exceptional prince access remain tightly focused in 44:1-3, while the next movement changes gate, visual event, and audience charge.
reviews.support: Accept Ezek.44.1-3 as the east-gate rule. Keep its corrective siblings hydrated, but do not merge a concise closure-and-prince provision with the north-gate glory and personnel rulings.
reviews.counterevidence: Extending the shut-gate rule through Ezek.44.14 was rejected because 44:4 relocates by the north gate, renews the glory sight, and begins a sanctuary-access indictment.

reviews.rationale: The movement establishes a general sanctuary-access correction grounded in past abominations; its location, vision, attention formula, and broad prohibition precede the class-specific consequences.
reviews.support: Keep Ezek.44.4-9 as the glory-and-access correction. It supplies the charge to which 44:10-14 responds, so both children require sibling visibility without erasing the narrowing seam.
reviews.counterevidence: Joining Ezek.44.4-9 either backward to the prince's east-gate rule or forward into the Levite penalty was rejected because 44:10 narrows the addressee class with 'but the Levites.'

reviews.rationale: A stable Levite subject governs fault, consequence, permitted tasks, disallowed approach, and custody duties; the next verse contrasts the faithful Zadokite priests.
reviews.support: Accept Ezek.44.10-14 as the Levite reassignment child between the access indictment and Zadokite register. Its adversative subject reset supplies the boundary while preserving causal hydration.
reviews.counterevidence: Absorbing the Levite ruling into the broader Ezek.44.4-9 access indictment was rejected because the text narrows from unauthorized entrants generally to one named ministerial class and its reassignment.

reviews.rationale: Diverse legal clauses accumulate as one office register: qualifications, conduct, public instruction, cultic purity, and livelihood all define the same priestly vocation.
reviews.support: Retain Ezek.44.15-31 as the Zadokite legal register. Internal topics deserve indexes, not independent chunks, because no replacement addressee or heading interrupts the governing priestly contrast.
reviews.counterevidence: Dividing at the clothing, marriage, judicial, or inheritance subsections was rejected because the Zadokite-priest subject and near-sanctuary service frame every rule through Ezek.44.31.

reviews.rationale: The lot-division protasis initiates a distributive register, spatial measurements relate each share, and the final command that princes cease dispossession states the allocation's social purpose.
reviews.support: Keep Ezek.45.1-8 as one land-allocation unit. Constituent parcels are meaningful list entries, but the opening division formula and closing justice demand require their joint presentation.
reviews.counterevidence: Separate chunks for priests, Levites, city, and prince in Ezek.45.1-8 were rejected because these constituencies are coordinated allocations within one contribution and land-justice arrangement.

reviews.rationale: Economic justice and cultic provision are linked by the same quantities and political addressee: honest standards lead directly to assessed dues and the prince's atoning festival responsibility.
reviews.support: Retain Ezek.45.9-17 as an economic-cultic regulation. Index the 45:13 transition, but do not separate the assessment formula from the measures that make it intelligible.
reviews.counterevidence: A cut at Ezek.45.13 between metrological standards and communal dues was rejected because the measures quantify the offerings and the prince's duty answers the people's contribution.

reviews.rationale: The unit is bounded by paired first- and seventh-day acts and a stated cleansing purpose; it finishes before the fourteenth-day Passover formula changes occasion and duration.
reviews.support: Accept Ezek.45.18-20 as the annual sanctuary-purification child. Its calendar neighbors remain visible, yet its paired dates and cleansing target constitute a complete prescription.
reviews.counterevidence: Merging Ezek.45.18-20 into the Passover rules beginning at 45:21 was rejected because the dates, purpose, and sanctuary-purification rite differ from the ensuing seven-day festival calendar.

reviews.rationale: Passover duration, daily offerings, oil quantities, and the analogous seventh-month feast form a two-festival annual instruction distinct from sanctuary cleansing and weekly gate rules.
reviews.support: Keep Ezek.45.21-25 as the paired festival child. Its opening fourteenth-day formula and closing seventh-month analogue define the unit more precisely than the larger calendar register.
reviews.counterevidence: Treating Ezek.45.21-25 as part of the first-and-seventh-day purification prescription was rejected because 45:21 resets date and festival, while 45:25 supplies a matched autumn observance.

reviews.rationale: Gate access, prince and people, weekly-monthly occasions, movement paths, and freewill offerings form one public worship protocol; the repeated morning rule that follows is narrower.
reviews.support: Retain Ezek.46.1-12 as the Sabbath, new-moon, and voluntary-offering regulation. The prince's freewill case completes the gate protocol before daily sacrifice becomes the subject.
reviews.counterevidence: Extending this regulation through the daily morning offering in Ezek.46.13-15 was rejected because 46:13 shifts to a direct second-person daily prescription with a different temporal cadence.

reviews.rationale: Animal, grain, oil, recurrence, and perpetuity are all governed by a single daily-morning prescription, whose closing summary repeats its temporal marker and sacrificial classification.
reviews.support: Accept Ezek.46.13-15 as the daily-offering child. It must stay beside 46:1-12 in calendar retrieval, but its daily cadence and second-person formulation justify separate indexing.
reviews.counterevidence: Attaching Ezek.46.13-15 to the preceding Sabbath and new-moon gate protocol was rejected because the addressee grammar, daily frequency, and compact offering recipe reset at 46:13.

reviews.rationale: The compact law moves from two contrasting beneficiaries to its public-policy rationale; the jubilee reversion and anti-expulsion command jointly protect inherited land.
reviews.support: Keep Ezek.46.16-18 as a single inheritance regulation. The closing prohibition interprets the preceding gift cases, so extracting either example would conceal the law's anti-displacement aim.
reviews.counterevidence: Dividing the son, servant, and anti-displacement clauses into separate cases was rejected because all three regulate how princely property may pass without eroding tribal holdings.

reviews.rationale: Two locations serve related but differentiated preparation functions; the guide deliberately shows both and ends by identifying who boils the people's sacrifices in the outer rooms.
reviews.support: Retain Ezek.46.19-24 as one guided kitchen tour. Internal location change should be indexed, while comparative purpose and uninterrupted guidance argue against isolated room inventories.
reviews.counterevidence: A break at Ezek.46.21 between the priest kitchen and four public-court kitchens was rejected because guide movement and repeated cooking-place language create one comparative functional-space tour.

reviews.rationale: Source, eastward movement, progressive crossings, return to the bank, interpretive question, healed waters, fisheries, and perpetual trees form one guided water-vision arc.
reviews.support: Keep Ezek.47.1-12 together. Neither the spectacular depth measurements nor the ecological catalogue is complete alone; the latter discloses what the former visionary movement means.
reviews.counterevidence: Cuts after the depth sequence at Ezek.47.5 or before ecological effects at 47:8 were rejected because the guide's question links measured growth to the water's interpreted life-giving consequences.

reviews.rationale: Territorial limits and eligible recipients are two dimensions of one allotment register; the resident clause repeatedly invokes inheritance and tribal assignment rather than changing topics.
reviews.support: Retain Ezek.47.13-23 as the boundary-and-eligibility register. Index the 47:20/21 transition, but keep resident inclusion attached to the land whose borders have just been defined.
reviews.counterevidence: A proposed ending at Ezek.47.20 after the geographic borders was rejected because 47:21-23 states who participates in distribution of the just-bounded land and serves as its legal coda.

reviews.rationale: Tribal names and border descriptions operate as coordinated entries rather than narrative episodes; Judah's portion closes the northern run immediately before the central contribution.
reviews.support: Keep Ezek.48.1-7 as the northern allotment list. Individual tribes remain addressable as entries, but retrieving them as standalone literary chunks would erase the ordered geographic sequence.
reviews.counterevidence: Making each repeated 'one portion' clause in Ezek.48.1-7 an independent unit was rejected because the heading, north-to-south order, and formulaic repetition define one list.

reviews.rationale: Repeated dimensions and adjacency statements interlock the parcels, while the contribution's placement between named tribes brackets the entire central-zone allocation.
reviews.support: Retain Ezek.48.8-22 as one coordinated central allocation. Sub-parcels should be indexed within the unit, since their sizes and locations only make sense in relation to one another.
reviews.counterevidence: Separate priest, Levite, city, and prince chunks within Ezek.48.8-22 were rejected because every subsection locates a constituent inside the same central sacred-civic zone.

reviews.rationale: Five parallel tribal portions complete the north-to-south arrangement and the colophon explicitly names the inheritance and tribes; neither city dimensions nor gate names belong to that list form.
reviews.support: Accept Ezek.48.23-29 as the southern allotment child. Keep the city-name sibling visible for book closure, but honor the 48:29 colophon as the end of the land register.
reviews.counterevidence: Continuing the tribal list into the city exits at Ezek.48.30 was rejected because the allotment colophon in 48:29 closes the distribution before a directional gate register begins.

reviews.rationale: Four directional sides, twelve gate names, a perimeter total, and the terminal city-name formula form a self-contained urban colophon that also supplies the book's final cadence.
reviews.support: Keep Ezek.48.30-35 as the city gate-and-name close. Its relation to the preceding allotment is essential, but the change from territorial portions to gates and naming warrants its own child.
reviews.counterevidence: Merging Ezek.48.30-35 backward into the southern tribal allotments was rejected because 48:29 already closes land distribution and 48:30 resets to city dimensions and gates.
